purpose: Define the durable release-plan envelope: its serialized shape, its canonical encoding, the two disk-state digests that bind it to the workspace it was planned from, the versions this build accepts, and the total validation that must pass before any consumer acts on it. This is the forge-neutral, process-neutral core that SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001B (CLI command modes) and SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C (GitHub Actions topology) both build on, so that a reviewed versioning decision can survive a process boundary without a CI cache, an untracked workspace file, or a silently recomputed fresh plan being treated as authoritative release intent.
scope: A new `PublishPlanEnvelope` type in `crates/callisto-model/src/envelope.rs` wrapping the existing `PublishPlan` (crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:27) as its payload; the canonical JSON encoding used for digest computation; the exhaustive, deterministically ordered input sets for `configDigest` and `inputDigest`; the accepted `schemaVersion` / `digestSchemeVersion` values and the rejection behavior for every other value; the total structural validation performed before any consumer mutates state; and a structural provenance table proving every envelope field is sourced from repository content or static configuration rather than the process environment. Digest computation and validation are pure functions of on-disk state plus the envelope bytes: they read no credentials, spawn no registry client, and perform no planning pass.
non_goals: Implementing the CLI command-mode separation, the plan-driven execution entry point, or the operation-status record. SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001B owns those; this spec defines only the envelope and the validation function they invoke.
Implementing any forge job topology or artifact handoff. SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C owns that.

Including `callisto_graph::plan::VersionPlan` (crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs:13) in the envelope. At last_verified_revision it derives only `Clone, Debug, Default` -- no `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, or `JsonSchema` -- `callisto-graph` carries no `schemars` dependency, and `plan_publish` consumes it purely as an in-process intermediate (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs:215-234, reading only `plan.bumps`). It is never serialized and is not part of the durable contract; the envelope payload is `PublishPlan` alone.

Cryptographically signing or attesting the envelope. The digests here bind a plan to observed disk state; they establish neither authorship nor non-repudiation, and no signature, in-toto attestation, or provenance statement is produced.
Committing transient plan files, CI outputs, or caches to the repository.
Replacing committed manifests, changelogs, release tags, or registry state as the durable records of a completed release. The envelope records intent; those remain the record of outcome.

Unifying the two `pre.json` read paths. `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:79` hardcodes `.changeset/pre.json` while the delete path at version.rs:254 resolves `[changesets].dir`; AC-002 hashes both paths so the digest is faithful to today's behavior, but reconciling the inconsistency is a separate change.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The serialized envelope is `PublishPlanEnvelope` (crates/callisto-model/src/envelope.rs), `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", deny_unknown_fields)]`, with exactly these fields: `schemaVersion` (u32, governs the envelope), `digestSchemeVersion` (u32), `sourceCommit` (the 40-character lowercase-hex git HEAD SHA observed at planning time, the same value `Workspace::git_access().head_sha()` returns at crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs:254), `configDigest` (64 lowercase hex characters), `inputDigest` (64 lowercase hex characters), `generatedAt`, and `plan` (a `PublishPlan`, which retains its own `schemaVersion` field, crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:28). `generatedAt` is RFC 3339 in UTC at whole-second precision with a literal `Z` suffix and no fractional part -- exactly `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, e.g. `2026-08-29T14:03:11Z`. `digestSchemeVersion` is incremented whenever the hashed input set or the canonicalization procedure changes, independently of `schemaVersion`, so a future config-shape change cannot silently produce a mismatched digest that wrongly accepts or rejects a plan. `PublishPlanEnvelope`, `PublishPlan`, and every nested payload type (`CratePublish`, `NpmPublish`, `NpmMainPublish`, `PypiPublish`, `ReleaseEntry`) carry `deny_unknown_fields`, so a field present in the received bytes but unknown to this build is a hard deserialization failure rather than a silent drop -- none of these types carries that attribute at last_verified_revision. Both digests are SHA-256 over a canonical encoding in which object keys are sorted lexicographically by Unicode scalar value at every nesting level, there is no insignificant whitespace, and a field whose value is absent (Rust `None`, or an empty `Vec` under `skip_serializing_if`) is omitted from the canonical form identically to a field that was never present in the source data -- the canonicalizer never emits an explicit null. Neither digest is computed over the envelope or any of its own fields, so the scheme is free of self-reference.

`configDigest` is SHA-256 over the canonical encoding of the object `{"files": [...]}`, where the array is ordered by `path` sorted lexicographically by Unicode scalar value, every `path` is workspace-root-relative using `/` separators, and each element is either `{"path": <path>, "sha256": <64 lowercase hex of the file's raw bytes>}` or `{"path": <path>, "absent": true}`. The path set is exactly and exhaustively: (1) `callisto.toml`; (2) `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; (3) `Cargo.toml`; (4) `package.json`; (5) `pyproject.toml`; (6) `.changeset/pre.json`; (7) `<changesets_dir>/pre.json` when the resolved `[changesets].dir` differs from `.changeset`; and (8) every file matching `<changesets_dir>/*.md` in a single non-recursive directory read, excluding exactly the name `README.md`. `<changesets_dir>` is the resolved `[changesets].dir` from `callisto.toml`, defaulting to `.changeset` (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:248-262). Entries (1) through (7) are a fixed list independent of what exists on disk: each one that is absent contributes an `absent: true` element, never a hard error, because every one of them is legitimately optional at run time -- `config::load` falls back to `RawConfig::default()` when `callisto.toml` is missing (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:231-244) and the membership readers treat a missing root manifest as admit-all (crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs). Entry (8) is an enumeration, so an absent or empty directory contributes no elements. A file that exists but whose bytes cannot be read -- a permission error, an I/O error, or a symlink loop -- is a hard error that terminates digest computation with a non-zero exit; it MUST NOT be recorded as absent, because absent and unreadable are distinct facts and conflating them would let a permissions change pass validation silently. Root `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, and `pyproject.toml` appear here because their workspace-membership tables govern package discovery; their per-package content also reaches `inputDigest` through resolved state, and that redundancy is intentional.

`inputDigest` is SHA-256 over the canonical encoding of the object `{"packages": [...]}`, where the array is sorted lexicographically by Unicode scalar value of each element's serialized `packageId`, and each element carries exactly these fields: `packageId` (the JSON form of `callisto_model::PackageId`); `manifestPaths` (workspace-root-relative manifest paths for that package, lexicographically sorted); `currentVersion` (the rendered `Version`, omitted when unknown); `publishTo` (rendered `PublishTarget` strings, lexicographically sorted); `dependencies` (sorted by `name` then `kind`, each `{"name", "kind", "spec"}` with `spec` omitted when none); `changelogPath` (workspace-root-relative, omitted when the package has none); and `role` (the rendered `ManifestRole`). This is exactly the manifest-derived state `plan_publish` consumes: identity and version from `Cargo.toml` `package.name`/`package.version`, `package.json` `name`/`version`, and `pyproject.toml` `project.name`/`project.version` with the poetry and flit fallbacks; `publishTo` from `Cargo.toml` `package.publish`, `package.json` `private`/`publishConfig`, and any `callisto.toml` `[[package]]`/`[[package-set]]` `publish-to` override (crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:306-399); dependency edges, which determine `publish_order`; the changelog path, which determines `ReleaseEntry.changelogSection`; and the role, which classifies npm platform versus main packages. Lockfiles are excluded because no lockfile content is read during planning -- `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, and `package-lock.json` are only stat'd for existence (crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs:421-443) and `Cargo.lock`, `uv.lock`, and `poetry.lock` are untouched until apply (crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:418-428). Git tag state is excluded because tag creation is an effect of executing this very plan, so hashing it would make a plan invalidate itself mid-execution; the commit the plan was made against is bound by `sourceCommit` instead. Because `inputDigest` is computed over resolved discovery output rather than over a file list, inputs that only influence which packages are discovered -- in-tree `.gitignore` files, honored by `WalkBuilder::git_ignore(true)` at crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs:42-43 -- are covered transitively by their effect on the package set.

This build accepts exactly `schemaVersion = 1` on the envelope, `digestSchemeVersion = 1`, and a payload `plan.schemaVersion` equal to `callisto_model::SCHEMA_VERSION` (crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:12, currently `1`). Any other value in any of those three fields -- higher, lower, non-integer, or absent -- terminates with a non-zero exit before any digest is recomputed and before any mutation is attempted. There is no compatibility shim, no field back-filling, and no best-effort acceptance of a lower version. The diagnostic carries exactly these fields: `field` (which of the three), `found` (the value read, or the literal `absent`), `supported` (the single value this build accepts), and `source` (the plan's origin -- the file path, or `-` for stdin).

The canonical encoder rejects any floating-point value (`f32` or `f64`) encountered while serializing the envelope, terminating digest computation with a non-zero exit and a diagnostic naming the JSON pointer of the offending value and the Rust type and field it came from. No envelope or payload type contains a floating-point field at last_verified_revision (verified across `PublishPlanEnvelope`, `PublishPlan`, `CratePublish`, `NpmPublish`, `NpmMainPublish`, `PypiPublish`, `ReleaseEntry`, and `NpmAccess`), so this path is unreachable today; the criterion exists so that introducing a float is a hard, immediate failure at digest time rather than a silent cross-platform digest divergence, and so no float-formatting standard needs to be specified for a case that cannot occur. A test asserts that canonicalizing a wrapper struct containing an `f64` returns an error rather than any encoded output.

Envelope validation is a total, fail-closed check that is STRUCTURAL with respect to the operation set and observation-driven only with respect to disk-state digests. Concretely: the envelope bytes are deserialized under the `deny_unknown_fields` types of AC-001 and re-serialized under AC-001's canonical encoding; `configDigest` and `inputDigest` are recomputed from currently observed disk state per AC-002 and AC-003 and compared for exact string equality against the envelope's values; `sourceCommit` is compared for exact equality against the git HEAD SHA observed at validation time; and `schemaVersion`, `digestSchemeVersion`, and payload `plan.schemaVersion` are checked per AC-004. The requested operation set -- every entry of `rustCrates`, `npmPlatformPackages`, `npmMainPackages`, `pypiPackages`, and `releases` -- is taken verbatim from the envelope and MUST NOT be independently re-derived, re-observed, or regenerated by a fresh planning pass; a test asserts the validation path invokes neither `callisto_graph::commands::plan_publish` nor `callisto_graph::commands::version::plan_version`. Recomputing the digests is observation of config and manifest state, which is precisely what those digests exist to bind; it is not observation of what should be published, and this distinction is what makes AC-006 compatible with SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001B's rule that plan-driven execution never recomputes a plan for itself. `generatedAt` is recorded for audit and is not compared. `PublishPlan::diagnostics` (crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:39) does not participate in the comparison: it is informational human-readable output, not part of the operation set being validated, and it is excluded from `inputDigest` for the same reason. For the fields that do participate, an omitted array and an explicit empty array are equal, not a mismatch -- `pypiPackages` carries `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`, so both forms deserialize to the same value and both re-serialize to omission -- and a test asserts a plan with `pypiPackages` omitted and one with `pypiPackages: []` produce byte-identical canonical encodings and equal digests. That equivalence is the only defaulting permitted for a participating field: any new participating field whose serde default is not identical to its canonical-omission form MUST be introduced together with a `schemaVersion` increment. Validation fails closed -- any error while recomputing current state (a present-but-unreadable file, an unparseable manifest, an unavailable git HEAD, a digest computation failure) is treated as a mismatch and blocks the consumer, never as a pass. On any mismatch the diagnostic identifies every mismatching or unrecomputable field, not just the first one found.

The envelope is structurally guaranteed to be secret-free by construction. A module `crates/callisto-model/src/plan_provenance.rs` declares `pub enum FieldSource { Manifest, CallistoConfig, GitRef, ComputedVersion, Constant }` -- an enumeration with no variant that can denote a process environment variable, a CLI credential flag, or any value flowing through the registry-authentication path, so an environment-sourced field is unrepresentable in the provenance table -- and `pub const PLAN_FIELD_PROVENANCE: &[(&str, &str, FieldSource)]` holding one `(type_name, serialized_field_name, source)` triple per field, with `serialized_field_name` in the camelCase form the type actually serializes. A test generates `schemars::schema_for!(PublishPlanEnvelope)` -- `schemars` is already a dependency of `callisto-model` (crates/callisto-model/Cargo.toml:28) and every type below already derives `JsonSchema` -- walks the generated schema's definitions for `PublishPlanEnvelope`, `PublishPlan`, `CratePublish`, `NpmPublish`, `NpmMainPublish`, `PypiPublish`, `ReleaseEntry`, and `NpmAccess`, and asserts both directions: every `(type, field)` in the generated schema has exactly one entry in `PLAN_FIELD_PROVENANCE`, and every entry in `PLAN_FIELD_PROVENANCE` names a field present in the generated schema. Adding a field without a provenance entry fails the first assertion; removing a field without removing its entry fails the second. The test lives in `callisto-model` alone, because every envelope and payload type lives in that crate and `VersionPlan` is excluded from the envelope per this spec's non_goals.

implementation_notes: Canonicalization (AC-001): `olpc-cjson` is a `serde_json::Formatter` already used in production by AWS's `tough` (TUF) crate, and is already present in Cargo.lock at 0.1.4 as a transitive dependency of `oci-client`. Apply it directly against the typed structs via `serde_json::Serializer::with_formatter`, avoiding an intermediate `serde_json::Value` and this workspace's `preserve_order` serde_json feature (which makes `Value` insertion-ordered, not sorted). `serde_json_canonicalizer` (strict RFC 8785 JCS) is a stricter but less production-proven alternative.

Float rejection (AC-005): olpc-cjson's canonical-JSON dialect has no float representation. If its `Formatter` implementation does not itself return an error from `write_f32`/`write_f64`, wrap it in a newtype `Formatter` that overrides both to return `io::Error` -- do not rely on the underlying crate's behavior without a test pinning it, since a silent fallback to `serde_json`'s default float formatting is exactly the cross-platform digest divergence AC-005 exists to prevent.

Hashing (AC-002, AC-003): `sha2` is present in Cargo.lock at both 0.10.9 and 0.11.0 but is not a direct dependency of any workspace crate. Add `sha2 = "0.11"` to `callisto-model` explicitly rather than relying on the transitive pin.

Omitted-vs-null (AC-001): a `#[serde(skip_serializing_if)]`-skipped field is invisible to any serde-Formatter-based canonicalizer by construction, satisfying 'omitted == never present' automatically. `PublishPlan::pypi_packages` and `PublishPlan::diagnostics` already carry `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]` (crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:33,38), so this path is live today. It does not by itself guarantee 'omitted == explicit null' -- that holds only as long as no field's `Option<T>` can serialize `Some(Value::Null)`. Worth a one-line comment at the point of digest computation.

deny_unknown_fields (AC-001): adding this attribute to `PublishPlan` and its nested types is a behavior change for the existing `callisto tag --plan` and `callisto filter-plan --plan` inputs (crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs:224,240), which today silently ignore unknown keys. That tightening is intended and in scope.

Config input set (AC-002): `callisto.toml` is the single configuration file, resolved as one `root.join("callisto.toml")` with no ancestor walk, no layering, no `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` path, and no per-package config file -- per-package settings are `[[package]]`/`[[package-set]]` blocks inside that one file (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:231-244, 350-485). There is no `[workspace.metadata.callisto]` table and no `callisto` key in package.json. `.changeset/config.json` is never read (only referenced as a reserved diagnostic at crates/callisto-model/src/diagnostic.rs:131) and is deliberately not in the hashed set.

Changeset enumeration (AC-002): `load_changesets` filters on `is_file() && extension == "md"` and then excludes `README.md` (crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs:48-58); the sibling exclusions for `config.json` and `pre.json` in that same condition are dead code, already unreachable behind the `.md` gate. The effective glob is `<changesets_dir>/*.md` minus `README.md`, non-recursive, which is what AC-002 specifies.

Manifest discovery (AC-003): `IgnoreWalkLocator` probes exactly three filenames per visited directory -- `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml` -- with `max_depth(32)`, `hidden(true)`, `git_ignore(true)`, `parents(false)`, and a hardcoded skip set of `target`, `node_modules`, `.git`, `.moon`, `dist` (crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs:18-146). No other manifest kind is enumerated.

Provenance table (AC-007): making the third tuple element a closed `FieldSource` enum rather than a free-form `&str` accessor description is what turns AC-007 from a documentation convention into a type-level guarantee -- a string description could name `std::env::var` and only a substring check would catch it, whereas the enum has no variant capable of expressing it.
